newsitem.title: ARMENIA: World Bank backs Armenian economic moves-official.
newsitem.headline: World Bank backs Armenian economic moves-official.

text.p: An official of the World Bank on Thursday gave strong backing to the reorganisation of Armenia's economic ministries by President Levon Ter-Petrosyan earlier in the week.

"We approve the structural changes that were made. This is the line the government began with several years ago and in the future it will be necessary to further curtail the number of government employees," said Vakhram Narsisyants, representative of the World Bank in Armenia.

Ter-Petrosyan signed a decree on Tuesday combining the Economy Ministry and Finance Ministry into a single entity - the Ministry of Finance and Economy. The Trade and Industry ministries were also amalgamated into a single Industry and Trade Ministry.
Narsisyants said the Economy Ministry had been little more than an superfluous successor to the Soviet-era state planning ministry known as Gosplan.
"Placing the Economy Ministry within the Finance Ministry will make it more effective. This is the case all over the world," he said in an interview.

"The goal of this is to make the goverment more lean. The private sector is expanding and the role of the government is becoming smaller. The government must act as a regulator and guarantee the growth of the economy," he said.

While most people in the landlocked former Soviet republic of 3.5 million are still poor, inflation has been greatly reduced, yearly economic growth is running at around five percent and once-crippling power cuts have been eliminated.
Narsisyants declined to give an assessment of the dismissals of Economy Minister Vakham Avenesyan and Industry Minister Ashot Safaryan, which were part of the President's decree.
The World Bank is due to begin talks with the government in the middle of June on issuing a $60 million structural adjustment credit to Armenia.
"I don't see any serious problems with the negotiations," he said. --Lawrence Sheets, Tbilisi newsroom +995-32 999-370
